question: Why is hospital waste such a big deal when it comes to controlling infections?

options.C: High microbial load and pathogenic risk

explanation: Hospital waste is dangerous mainly because it carries loads of harmful germs that can cause sickness. You've got this! [learn more](GST114_U2_T7#GST114_U2_T7_h1)

question: Why do organic waste materials in the hospital need to be handled right away?

options.A: They are more expensive to incinerate than plastics
options.B: They damage heavy-duty municipal waste trucks
options.C: They serve as breeding grounds for harmful microorganisms
options.D: They take longer to decompose in landfills

explanation: Wet organic waste gives bacteria and fungi a cozy place to multiply fast. Sorting it quickly keeps everyone safe! [learn more](GST114_U2_T7#GST114_U2_T7_h1)

question: Expired medicines and unused vaccines belong to which group of healthcare waste?
explanation: Any drugs or chemical agents that can't be used anymore are sorted neatly under pharmaceutical waste. [learn more](GST114_U2_T7#GST114_U2_T7_h2)

question: If you throw away a used surgical scalpel blade, which waste category does it go into?
explanation: Anything that can cut or prick skin is a 'sharp' and needs a special puncture-proof container. Safety first! [learn more](GST114_U2_T7#GST114_U2_T7_h2)

question: Who is most at risk when a needle is carelessly thrown into a regular trash bin?
explanation: Exposed needles are dangerous traps for the nurses and cleaners handling the trash bags. Always use safety boxes! [learn more](GST114_U2_T7#GST114_U2_T7_h3)

question: Which bloodborne germ is most commonly spread through an accidental needlestick injury?
explanation: Hepatitis B passes very easily through accidental pricks compared to many other blood infections. Great reason to stay vaccinated and careful! [learn more](GST114_U2_T7#GST114_U2_T7_h3)

question: At what exact point in the hospital routine should waste sorting (segregation) happen?
explanation: Always sort your waste right where you use it—at the bedside or treatment tray—to avoid mistakes later. [learn more](GST114_U2_T7#GST114_U2_T7_h4)

question: You just cleaned a wound and have cotton balls soaked in blood. Which bin do they go into?
explanation: Items soaked in blood or body fluids always go into the yellow infectious bag. You're getting the hang of this! [learn more](GST114_U2_T7#GST114_U2_T7_h4)

question: What is the main job of an autoclave in a hospital?
explanation: An autoclave uses hot steam under pressure to kill all germs on medical tools. It's a nurse's best friend for sterilization! [learn more](GST114_U2_T7#GST114_U2_T7_h5)

question: Why do we use high-temperature burning (incineration) for body tissues like placentas?

options.A: It prepares the material for recycling into plastic products
options.B: It prevents the autoclave from rusting due to high moisture
options.C: It completely destroys tissues and eliminates visual or biological recognition
options.D: It is the cheapest method available for processing liquids

explanation: Incineration completely and respectfully destroys anatomical parts while stopping any disease from spreading. [learn more](GST114_U2_T7#GST114_U2_T7_h5)

question: Why is recapping used needles with two hands a dangerous habit?

options.A: High risk of accidental needlestick injuries
options.C: Damage to the sterile needle tip
options.D: Contamination of the outer barrel with drugs

explanation: Trying to put the cap back on by hand often leads to accidentally pricking your own fingers. Never recap used needles! [learn more](GST114_U2_T7#GST114_U2_T7_h6)

question: Your safety box in the treatment room is getting full. What should you do?

options.A: Leave it open until the very top edge is completely packed
options.B: Press the needles down firmly with a pen to create more space
options.C: Seal and replace the box when it reaches three-quarters full
options.D: Transfer some needles into a regular black polythene bag

explanation: Safety boxes are safest when sealed at 3/4 full so nobody gets poked by overflowing sharps. Well done! [learn more](GST114_U2_T7#GST114_U2_T7_h6)

question: Which Nigerian agency is responsible for enforcing environmental rules, including hospital waste?
explanation: NESREA ensures that environmental laws protecting our communities and hospitals are strictly followed. [learn more](GST114_U2_T7#GST114_U2_T7_h7)

question: What is a common challenge hospitals in Nigeria face with waste management?

options.A: Unreliable power supply for operating incinerators
options.B: Too many functional autoclaves in rural clinics
options.C: A complete absence of infectious waste generation
options.D: An excess of well-trained environmental health officers

explanation: Power outages can sometimes disrupt large hospital incinerators, making creative waste management super important in our clinics. [learn more](GST114_U2_T7#GST114_U2_T7_h7)
